key_insight: AI is not just speeding up science; it is turning research into an automated pipeline, with major risks for expertise, transparency, and governance.
engineering_relevance: For computational science teams, the paper highlights that AI-enabled discovery systems need strong human oversight, provenance tracking, and error controls to avoid scaling mistakes along with productivity.
method: Frames AI-driven science as a shift from craft-based research to pipeline-based research
Examines seven consequences: competence loss, opacity, peer-review overload, weak evidence for paradigm shifts, agenda capture, error compounding, and community bifurcation
Uses the U.S. DOE Genesis Mission as a concrete example of this broader transformation
evidence_signal: The abstract is an argument-based essay drawing on the Genesis Mission and conceptual analysis rather than presenting new experimental data or benchmark evaluation.
watch_item: Closed-loop AI research pipelines may compound systematic errors if automated outputs are not rigorously validated by human experts.
paper_title: The Industrialization of Research ; On AI-Driven Science and Its Consequences
